scope: Source and preserved ELF inspection only; no tests/builds/VM or timing

baseline.path_condition: waiting, nonzero; candidate specifically READY with budget greater than one

once.path_condition: waiting, nonzero; candidate specifically READY with budget greater than one

verified_changes: One READY publication byte store and INIT guard before incoming-link publication, once per ordinary queued invocation.

Within-budget candidate loop executes state validation and budget maintenance even without expiry. Current-task GS fetch is hoisted before the loop, and the within-budget path adds no per-iteration memory load beyond the same notification byte.
First private head adds INIT-to-WAIT CAS. Full-word gate changes preserve WITHDRAW by CAS and admission uses HELD-to-COMBINER CAS. These are head/epoch costs.
Node count/key/generation enter/exit tracking and tail exchange already exist in baseline; they are not entirely new work.
bounded_hypothesis: Keep every state check and expiry/withdrawal rule, but separate finite initial-budget polling from post-expiry polling to avoid redundant budget-zero test/branch on each initial poll. This is a design hypothesis only; emitted savings and performance require separate validation.
limits: Nine more architectural instructions on the selected steady polling path are not nine cycles or measured instructions per completed operation. Poll counts are not available.
The matched whole-client +42.8% retired-instruction result has no per-function retired-instruction attribution.

Separate mode2 sessions reporting all wait episodes completed within their helper-loop budget do not prove zero expiry in uninstrumented perf sessions. The fraction counts episodes, not CPU-time share.
Flat cycles sampling with skid identifies neighborhoods; waiting amplification can be downstream of slower completion elsewhere.
No expectation of latency or throughput improvement is established for the proposed two-phase loop.
